questions.q: What are the four validation checks this lesson says a system must pass before returning to production?
options: A single confirmation that the restore from backup completed without errors
A password reset, a reboot, a backup, and a status email to management
Patch confirmation, a persistence re-check, a clean vulnerability scan targeting the exploited weakness, and a defined monitoring window
Only a general antivirus scan with no other checks required
questions.explain: Validation is four specific, separate checks, not a single pass/fail step or a general good-enough feeling.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat 'patch confirmation' as its own distinct check, separate from simply pushing the update?
options: Pushing a patch automatically guarantees it installed correctly every time
Patches never actually need to be confirmed once they are scheduled
A failed or pending patch installation can look identical to a successful one from the outside, so it has to be verified as actually installed and active
Patch confirmation is only relevant for cloud-hosted servers, not on-premises ones
questions.explain: Scheduling or pushing a patch isn't the same as confirming it's actually installed and running on the live system.

questions.q: Why does validation re-run the same persistence checks from Lesson 17, even on hosts already eradicated?
options: Because persistence checks have no real value and are only done for documentation
Because eradication work done under time pressure is worth re-verifying rather than trusting on the first pass, and a missed foothold wouldn't otherwise surface until the system is live again
Because PowerShell commands expire after a single use and must be run twice
Because the first eradication pass is always assumed to have failed
questions.explain: Re-checking catches anything the first pass missed, before the system is back in production where a missed foothold matters most.

questions.q: What distinguishes a 'clean vulnerability scan' in this lesson's validation step from a general health scan?
options: It is run by an outside auditor rather than the internal SOC
It replaces the need for a monitoring window entirely
It only checks CPU and memory usage on the server
It specifically targets the exact CVE or weakness that was exploited and must come back with zero criticals for that finding
questions.explain: The scan has to be targeted at the specific vulnerability the attacker actually exploited, not a generic scan.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what commonly causes real IR teams to rush or skip validation, and what is the real cost of doing so?
options: Validation is skipped because it is legally prohibited in most organizations
Time pressure and the assumption that a clean-looking restore means everything is fine — the cost is the same incident reopening later, sometimes after the team believed it was already closed
There is no real cost to skipping validation if the backup was already confirmed clean
Validation is rushed only when no monitoring tools are available at all
questions.explain: Rushing validation under time pressure is common and rarely dramatic in the moment, but it risks the same incident reopening undetected.
